source_refs.note: Exercise 1.3, Question 8: Exercise 1.3 questions, book page 11

blocks.prompt: 8 Find a polynomial of degree 4 with zeros \(4,\ -4,\ 1+i,\ 1-i\) and satisfying \(P(2)=72\).
blocks.explanation: We build a polynomial from its zeros: each zero \(r\) gives a factor \((z-r)\), and \(P(z)=a(z-z_{1})(z-z_{2})\cdots\) with an unknown number \(a\) in front. The extra condition fixes \(a\). Then expand and check. Here \(1+i\) and \(1-i\) are a conjugate pair.
steps:
Step 1: Multiply the real pair
\[(z-4)(z+4)=z^{2}-16\]
Why: Difference of squares.

Step 2: Multiply the conjugate pair
\[(z-1-i)(z-1+i)=(z-1)^{2}-i^{2}\]
\[=z^{2}-2z+1+1\]
\[=z^{2}-2z+2\]
Why: Treat \((z-1)\) as one block \(A\): \((A-i)(A+i)=A^{2}-i^{2}\).

Check: P(2)
\[-48+48+168-192+96=72\]
Why: The condition holds.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (page 297) prints this answer under the label 7, as \(x=-3z^{4}+6z^{3}+42z^{2}-96z+96\). It is the answer to Question 8, and it should read \(P(z)=\) rather than \(x=\). The polynomial itself is correct.
